results.title: [2303.03758] Patched Diffusion Models for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Brain MRI
results.content: arxiv logo > eess > arXiv:2303.03758. # Title:Patched Diffusion Models for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Brain MRI. View a PDF of the paper titled Patched Diffusion Models for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Brain MRI, by Finn Behrendt and 4 other authors. > Abstract:The use of supervised deep learning techniques to detect pathologies in brain MRI scans can be challenging due to the diversity of brain anatomy and the need for annotated data sets. An alternative approach is to use unsupervised anomaly detection, which only requires sample-level labels of healthy brains to create a reference representation. To accomplish this, generative models are needed to create anatomically consistent MRI scans of healthy brains. In this paper, we propose a method that reformulates the generation task of diffusion models as a patch-based estimation of healthy brain anatomy, using spatial context to guide and improve reconstruction. We evaluate our approach on data of tumors and multiple sclerosis lesions and demonstrate a relative improvement of 25.1% compared to existing baselines.
